newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to crack down on officials overseas.
newsitem.headline: Australia to crack down on officials overseas.

text.p: Australia said on Thursday it would impose strict controls on the behaviour of officials posted overseas, after a government inquiry criticised the handling of damaging child-sex allegations against diplomats.
Foreign Minister Alexander Downer, declaring paedophilia would not be tolerated in his department, said the foreign service must now clean up its image.

The year-long, closed probe found the service had mishandled child-sex charges against diplomats, with one case taking a decade to resolve, and urged prompt and decisive action over future allegations.
"What we need is, I think, the reputation of the Australian diplomatic service cleaned up," Downer said in a radio interview. "Some damage was done.
"The important thing now is that everything that can be exposed has been exposed."
The inquiry studied 15 allegations against 10 officers, but was not authorised to recommend any action. Evidence was instead referred to police.
"The community, the agencies and the officers concerned are now bearing the heavy consequences of this sad saga. It is time for a fresh start to be made," said the report.
Downer supported the inquiry's recommendation that a code of conduct be drafted to control the behaviour of all officials and their families posted overseas by any department or agency.

The inquiry's report did not set out a code, but said it should ensure respect for local laws and culture and ensure that officials or their families moderated their behaviour if it could damage Australia's reputation.

The inquiry said there had been no official cover-up of child-sex allegations, but added the Foreign Affairs Department had been lax in dealing with charges, putting privacy and corporate image ahead of resolving the issue.
Downer conceded problems with the department "over the years", but said the department had improved its performance.
"People will be charged if there's evidence against them," he said.

Downer ordered the inquiry in May, 1996, after a series of allegations diplomats were involved in child-sex rings in Asia, had sent child pornography through diplomatic mail, used aid money to buy access to children in orphanages in Asian countries and that the department had covered up the scandals.
The report found no evidence aid money had been misused.
One diplomat, former ambassador to Cambodia John Holloway, was charged with having sex with two boys under 16 while in Cambodia. But that case was thrown out of court last year.
